cs.t: I totally agree, I own a few fountain pens and Midori notebooks and for my lecture notes I just enter flow state using those. I've recently gotten an iPad and the most effective use case for it is to open up an infinite canvas and do active recall by drawing everything from (mostly) memory allowing me to find more connections, avenues to explore, and debate an idea. Eventually, I have to put those connections back into prose but I haven't gotten to that yet.

I like writing much better,[1] and after a fair share of Moleskin, Field Notes, and a long streak with Muji, I’m now blown away by Midori. I have already gotten a few, and I’m going to get a lot more. The tactile ‘scratch’ of the fountain pen on the Midori Paper is so soothing, it makes me feel like I’m a poet even when I’m writing down the most mundane idea that I just had. :-)  https://brajeshwar.com/2025/notes/
cs.th: As a developer, my most important tools are a pen and a notebook
